messages:
maria: incident-bot triggered pager — PagerDuty alert: Inference service: suspicious debug dump uploaded to S3 containing possible auth header snippets. paging oncall.
incident-bot: Pager alert - Severity: high - owner: maria (oncall) - incident_id=INC-1961234567
maria: observed in initial index: debug forwarder wrote `inf-debug-20260320.log` to s3://redwood-temp/dumps at ~10:12 UTC. suspect contains raw auth fragments.
devon: copying a redacted sample from the object for triage:
```
[2026-03-20T10:12:01Z] DEBUG inference: request_id=abc123 user=tenant-42 path=/v1/generate auth="k=sk-1a2b3c..." prompt_len=120
```
sre-jen: who has write access to that bucket? if headers are in there that's a secret exposure. start rotation plan and lock bucket.
maria: @ops-alex can you confirm whether this was an internal CI deploy or an external forwarder? tagging sec + legal.
ops-alex: investigating now. preliminary: forwarder lambda in CI ran with DEBUG_UPLOAD=true for a one-off deploy job. bucket redwood-temp had ACL accidentally set to public for ~4m.
sec-bot: ACTION REQUIRED: rotate any service tokens potentially exposed. Recommended command (ops): `aws s3api put-bucket-acl --bucket redwood-temp --acl private` and snapshot objects to forensics bucket.
maria: agreed. immediate runbook: 1) secure bucket (ops) 2) snapshot + preserve objects (forensics) 3) rotate affected tokens (devops) 4) quick customer-impact triage (cs/legal). who owns token rotation?
devon: rotating CI deploy token svc:ci-deployer now. will update Secrets Manager and restart runners. ETA ~8m. pushing infra change `rotate/ci-deployer-1961234567`.
sre-jen: add temporary deny rules on edge for request_id prefix `abc123` and rate-limit the source IPs. also run quick grep to find other dumps.
legal-sam: looped in. do not delete any objects; preserve integrity. we need a chain-of-custody for forensics before any external notice.
ops-alex: bucket ACL corrected to private. found 3 objects created during window. copying objects to `s3://forensics/inference/1961234567/` now.
devon: token rotation complete. Secrets Manager updated, services restarted. CI runners validated.
sec-bot: SUGGESTION: run a search for `sk-` or `ak-` patterns across recent uploads and logs, and rotate any long-lived keys found.
sre-jen: S3 access logs show 5 GETs from external IP ranges during the ACL window. flagging for intel. if those were enumerations we need to assume exfil may have occurred.
maria: initial customer-impact: two tenants (dev accounts) issued requests in the window. no evidence yet of production customer data, but treat as high-confidence secret exposure until proven otherwise.
legal-sam: preserve timelines, collect who had access to the CI job, and draft notification template but hold until scope confirmed.
ops-alex: forensics copy complete. snapshot metadata saved.
devon: pushed a small infra guard: default DEBUG_UPLOAD=false and gate to allowlist of internal dev buckets. PR: infra#4823.
sre-jen: next actions: 1) rotate any other service keys that used the same deploy principal, 2) add automated scrub to debug dumps to remove auth headers, 3) add CI check to prevent public ACLs on debug buckets.
maria: creating a ticket and scheduling 1hr post-incident sync. action owners: ops-alex (bucket lock + forensics), devon (rotate tokens + infra PR), sre-jen (edge block + logs grep), legal-sam (cust impact + comms).
legal-sam: once we confirm no external data retrieval beyond the 5 GETs we can scope notifications; otherwise prepare customer notice.
maria: thanks everyone. please ping this thread if you find new evidence. I'll update the incidents channel with a consolidated timeline in 30m. :thumbsup:
